name: Steak & Ale Pie
blurb: Slow-cooked beef in ale gravy under a puff pastry lid.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato purée, 440ml brown ale, 400ml beef stock
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown in batches.
Soften the veg, stir in the purée, add the ale and reduce, then the stock and herbs.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours; cool.
Fill a pie dish, top with pastry, glaze and vent, and bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes.

name: Gammon with Parsley Sauce
blurb: Poached gammon joint with a proper parsley white sauce, mash and greens.
ingredients: Sauce: 40g butter, 40g cornflour, 500ml of the cooking liquor + milk, big bunch of parsley
method: Simmer the gammon with the onion, bay and peppercorns for about 1.5 hours (25 min per 500g).
Rest, then carve.
Make the sauce with butter, cornflour and the strained liquor topped up with milk; stir in the chopped parsley.
Serve the gammon with mash, cabbage and lots of parsley sauce.

name: Faggots with Onion Gravy & Mushy Peas
blurb: Herby pork meatballs baked in gravy — proper old-school comfort food.
ingredients: 80g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1 tsp sage, 1 tsp thyme
Onion gravy: 2 onions, 1 tbsp flour, 600ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
Mushy peas and mash to serve
method: Mix the pork, livers, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and herbs; roll into large balls.
Brown, then set aside. Caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire.
Nestle the faggots into the gravy and bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes.
Serve with mushy peas and mash.

name: Liver, Bacon & Onion Gravy
blurb: Quick-seared calf's or lamb's liver with crisp bacon and a sticky onion gravy.
ingredients: 2 tbsp flour, 600ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Fry the bacon until crisp; set aside. Cook the onions in the fat until golden.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Dust the liver in seasoned flour and sear 1-2 minutes each side — keep it pink.
Return the bacon, nestle in the liver and serve with mash.

name: Bangers & Champ
blurb: Grilled sausages on spring-onion mash with a mountain of onion gravy.
ingredients: 900g potatoes, 6 spring onions, 60g butter, 100ml warm milk
Gravy: 3 onions, 1 tbsp cornflour, 600ml beef stock, 1 tsp Dijon, Worcestershire
method: Grill or fry the sausages slowly until browned all over.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter and milk; beat in the softened spring onions.
Cook the onions low and slow, add the cornflour, then the stock, mustard and Worcestershire.
Serve the sausages on the champ, drowned in gravy.

name: Smoked Haddock Fish Pie
blurb: Smoked and white fish in a herby sauce under cheesy mash.
method: Poach the fish in the milk with bay for 4 minutes; lift out and flake, keeping the milk.
Make a white sauce with butter, flour and the infused milk; stir in herbs.
Fold in the fish, peas and egg; tip into a dish.
Top with seasoned mash and cheddar; bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes.

name: Corned Beef Hash Pie
blurb: Corned beef, potato and onion baked under shortcrust — a chip-shop classic at home.
method: Fry the onions, add the potatoes, corned beef, stock and Worcestershire; thicken with cornflour and cool.
Line a pie dish with two-thirds of the pastry.
Fill, top with the rest of the pastry, seal, glaze and vent.
Bake at 190C fan for 35-40 minutes until golden.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Baked Potatoes
blurb: Fluffy jackets loaded with sharp cauliflower cheese and a crunchy top.
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes.
Blanch the cauliflower 4 minutes; make a cheese sauce with butter, cornflour, milk, most of the cheese and the mustard.
Split the potatoes, fluff, and pile with the cauliflower cheese.
Top with crumbs and the rest of the cheese; grill 5 minutes.

name: Homemade Scampi & Chips
blurb: Breadcrumbed langoustine tails with chips, peas and tartare.
ingredients: 500g raw peeled langoustine or large prawn tails
Tartare: 5 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 1 tsp capers, lemon
method: Roast the chips (tossed in oil) at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes.
Coat the tails in flour, egg then breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and cooked; drain.
Serve with the chips, peas, tartare and lemon.

name: Chicken Kiev
blurb: Crumbed chicken breast that bursts with garlic-parsley butter.
ingredients: 100g soft butter, 4 garlic cloves, big handful of parsley, squeeze of lemon
Mash or new potatoes and greens to serve
method: Beat the butter with the garlic, parsley and lemon; shape into a log and freeze until firm.
Cut a pocket in each breast and push in a chunk of the butter; seal well.
Coat in flour, egg then panko (double the egg and crumb layer).
Fry to colour, then bake at 190C fan for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.

name: Veggie Sausage Toad in the Hole
blurb: Meat-free sausages in crisp Yorkshire batter with red onion gravy.
ingredients: Gravy: 2 red onions, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml vegetable stock, 1 tsp balsamic, Marmite
method: Whisk the batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oil and sausages in a roasting tin at 220C fan for 8 minutes.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the door.
Caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock, balsamic and a little Marmite; simmer to a gravy.

name: Lentil Cottage Pie
blurb: Rich lentil and mushroom mince topped with golden mash — no one misses the meat.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tbsp Marmite, 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 300ml stock
method: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms for 12 minutes.
Add the purée, Marmite, tomatoes, lentils, stock and thyme; simmer 25 minutes until thick.
Top with olive-oil mash and rough up the surface.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Pork Chops with Apple & Cider
blurb: Pan-fried chops with a cream, cider and apple sauce, and mash.
ingredients: Few sage leaves, mash and greens to serve
method: Season and fry the chops for 4 minutes each side; rest.
Soften the onion and apple in the pan, add the sage.
Pour in the cider and reduce by half, then the cream and mustard.
Return the chops and any juices; serve with mash and greens.

name: Salmon Fishcakes
blurb: Flaked salmon and mash patties, crumbed and fried, with a lemon mayo.
ingredients: 3 spring onions, 2 tbsp chopped dill, zest of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp capers
Lemon mayo and salad to serve
method: Mix the salmon, mash, spring onions, dill, lemon zest and capers; season and shape into 8 cakes. Chill 20 minutes.
Coat in flour, egg then breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry for 3-4 minutes each side until golden and hot through.
Serve with lemon mayo and a green salad.

name: Welsh Rarebit with Poached Egg
blurb: Grown-up cheese on toast under ale-and-mustard sauce, with a runny egg on top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 egg yolk
method: Make a thick paste with butter, flour and ale; off the heat stir in the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire and yolk.
Toast the bread one side, spread the mixture on the other, and grill until dark and bubbling.
Poach the eggs.
Serve the rarebit topped with a poached egg.

name: Individual Beef Wellingtons
blurb: Fillet steaks with mushroom duxelles and prosciutto in crisp puff pastry.
method: Sear the seasoned steaks 1 minute each side; cool and brush with mustard.
Fry the mushrooms until all the moisture has gone; cool.
Lay prosciutto on cling film, spread with duxelles, sit the steak on top and wrap tightly; chill 20 minutes.
Wrap each in pastry, glaze, and bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes for medium-rare; rest 8 minutes.

name: Quick Sausage Cassoulet
blurb: Sausages, bacon and white beans in a rich tomato-thyme sauce with a crumb top.
ingredients: 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 200ml stock, 1 tsp thyme
method: Brown the sausages and lardons in a casserole.
Add the onion and garlic, then the tomatoes, beans, stock and thyme.
Simmer 25 minutes, then top with the breadcrumbs and dots of butter.
Bake at 200C fan for 15 minutes until the crumb is golden; scatter with parsley.

name: Roast Chicken Crown with All the Trimmings
blurb: A chicken crown roasted fast, with roast potatoes, stuffing, carrots and gravy.
ingredients: 1kg potatoes for roasting, 4 tbsp goose fat
Gravy: 1 tbsp flour, 400ml chicken stock, splash of white wine
method: Rub the crown with butter, thyme and lemon; roast at 190C fan for 55-65 minutes until 70C.
Parboil and roughen the potatoes; roast in hot fat 45-55 minutes.
Bake the stuffing balls; boil the carrots, steam the greens.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes; make gravy in the tin. Carve and serve.

name: Cheese & Onion Pasties
blurb: Buttery shortcrust parcels of cheddar, potato and softened onion.
method: Mix the potato, onion, cheese and mustard with a splash of milk; season well.
Roll the pastry and cut into 4 circles.
Pile filling on one half, fold and crimp into pasties.
Glaze with egg and bake at 190C fan for 30-35 minutes until golden.

name: Hunter's Chicken
blurb: Chicken breasts wrapped in bacon, topped with barbecue sauce and melted cheese.
ingredients: Chips or jacket potatoes and salad to serve
method: Wrap each chicken breast in 2 rashers of bacon.
Sear in an ovenproof pan to colour the bacon.
Spoon over the barbecue sauce and scatter with cheese.
Bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the cheese golden.

name: Lancashire Hotpot
blurb: Sliced lamb and onions under a lid of overlapping, buttery potato slices.
ingredients: 1 tbsp flour, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves
method: Toss the lamb in seasoned flour and brown, then layer with onions and carrots in a casserole.
Add the thyme, bay, stock and Worcestershire.
Overlap the potato slices on top, brush with butter and season.
Cover and cook at 160C fan for 1.5 hours, then uncover for 30 minutes to crisp the top.

name: Fish Finger Wraps
blurb: Crispy fish fingers, lettuce and tartare rolled in a soft tortilla — dinner in 15.
ingredients: Tartare: 4 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, squeeze of lemon
method: Bake or grill the fish fingers until crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Spread with tartare and pile on lettuce, cucumber and the fish fingers.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.

name: Minute Steak with Chips & Peppercorn Sauce
blurb: Thin fast-fried steak, oven chips and a creamy peppercorn sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 1 shallot, 150ml beef stock, 100ml double cream, 1 tbsp green peppercorns, 1 tsp Dijon, splash of brandy
method: Roast the chips at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes.
Fry the seasoned steaks 1 minute each side; rest.
Soften the shallot, add the brandy, then stock, cream, peppercorns and mustard; simmer to a coating sauce.
Serve the steak with chips, sauce and watercress.

name: Tomato Soup & Extra-Cheese Toastie
blurb: Silky tomato soup with a griddled three-cheese toastie for dunking.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp sugar, 400ml stock
Toastie: 4 slices bread, 60g cheddar, 40g mozzarella, 20g Parmesan, butter
method: Soften the onion and garlic, add the purée, tomatoes, sugar and stock; simmer 15 minutes and blitz.
Season and add a splash of cream and torn basil.
Butter the bread outside, fill with the cheeses, and griddle until golden and molten.
Serve the soup with the toastie cut into fingers.
